sEn: AI is accelerating both vulnerability discovery and exploitation in a self-reinforcing loop, leaving defenders without a durable advantage and making urgent preparation essential.
sZh: AI 正以自我强化的循环同时加速漏洞发现与利用，使防御方难以保持持久优势，因此亟需紧急备战。
absEn: This article examines the escalating cybersecurity crisis driven by AI, centering on a critical PHP vulnerability discovered by GPT-5.6 Sol that had existed for 14 years and was exploited before a patch could be deployed. The author argues that AI is simultaneously accelerating the discovery of new vulnerabilities and enabling attackers to exploit existing ones at scale, creating a self-reinforcing loop that is going vertical. While defenders happened to find the PHP flaw first, the eleven-week lead proved insufficient, suggesting defenders may not hold a durable advantage. The piece concludes that organizations must urgently prepare for AI-enabled attacks rather than wait, that current access policies for defensive tools are too conservative, and that the race between attackers and defenders has passed the point of no return, making it essential that defenders mostly win.
absZh: 本文探讨了由 AI 驱动的不断升级的网络安全危机，核心是 GPT-5.6 Sol 发现的一个已存在 14 年之久的 PHP 关键漏洞——该漏洞在补丁部署前便已被利用。作者认为，AI 既在加速发现新漏洞，也在让攻击者能够大规模利用现有漏洞，形成一个不断升级、正走向垂直增长的自我强化循环。尽管防御方恰好先发现了这个 PHP 漏洞，但十一周的领先时间仍被证明不够，这表明防御方可能无法保持持久优势。文章最后指出，各组织必须紧急为 AI 赋能的攻击做好准备，而非坐等；当前防御工具的访问政策过于保守；攻击者与防御者之间的竞赛已越过不可逆转的临界点，因此防御方必须大体上获胜。

contrib.en: GPT-5.6 Sol discovered a 14-year-old critical PHP vulnerability, but exploitation began before patching completed.
contrib.zh: GPT-5.6 Sol 发现了一个存在 14 年的 PHP 关键漏洞，但在补丁完成前漏洞已被利用。

contrib.en: AI accelerates both discovery of new vulnerabilities and exploitation of existing ones at scale, creating a self-reinforcing loop.
contrib.zh: AI 同时加速新漏洞的发现和现有漏洞的大规模利用，形成自我强化的循环。

contrib.en: Defenders found the PHP flaw first with an 11-week lead, yet this proved insufficient to prevent exploitation.
contrib.zh: 防御者率先发现 PHP 漏洞并拥有 11 周领先时间，但这仍不足以阻止漏洞被利用。

contrib.en: Current access policies for defensive AI tools are too conservative; broader access with monitoring is needed.
contrib.zh: 当前防御性 AI 工具的访问政策过于保守；需要在监控下扩大访问权限。

contrib.en: The attacker-defender race has passed the point of no return; defenders must mostly win.
contrib.zh: 攻击者与防御者的竞赛已过不可逆转的临界点；防御者必须基本获胜。

contrib.en: Organizations should urgently prepare for AI-enabled attacks rather than wait, as the situation will worsen first.
contrib.zh: 组织应紧急准备应对 AI 驱动的攻击而非等待，因为情况会先恶化。

limits.en: The 11-week lead was insufficient, suggesting defenders may not hold a durable advantage over attackers.
limits.zh: 11 周的领先时间不足，表明防御者可能无法对攻击者保持持久优势。

limits.en: The vulnerability was found by a model behind the public frontier, so attackers could plausibly have found it first.
limits.zh: 该漏洞由落后于公开前沿的模型发现，因此攻击者有可能先找到它。

limits.en: Open-weight models like GLM-5.3 are strong cyber attackers, and open model capabilities may outpace patching ability.
limits.zh: 像 GLM-5.3 这样的开放权重模型是强大的网络攻击者，开放模型能力可能超过修补能力。

limits.en: There is no clear line between user-authorized agentic behavior and cyberattacks, making bank defenses difficult.
limits.zh: 用户授权的智能体行为与网络攻击之间没有明确界限，使银行防御困难。

limits.en: Slowing the red queen race is difficult; the balance between diffusing capabilities and maintaining defender advantage remains unresolved.
limits.zh: 减缓红皇后竞赛很困难；在扩散能力与保持防御者优势之间的平衡仍未解决。

paras.en: Multiple sources using GPT-5.6 Sol identified a critical flaw in PHP. Okay, identified two critical flaws in PHP. The plan was to deploy the patch first before announcing the flaw, but the embargo on the fix got broken more than six hours in advance, so here we are.
paras.zh: 多个使用 GPT-5.6 Sol 的来源识别出了 PHP 中的一个严重漏洞。好吧，是识别出了 PHP 中的两个严重漏洞。原计划是先部署补丁再公布漏洞，但修复的禁发期提前六个多小时被打破，于是就有了现在这个局面。

paras.en: They may have been in a rush due to attackers finding the exploit. Amazon reports that this was happening as early as October 17, four days before disclosure. We are fortunate that this did not scale far larger than it did.
paras.zh: 他们可能因为攻击者已经发现了该漏洞利用方式而仓促行事。亚马逊报告称，这一情况早在 10 月 17 日就已发生，即披露前四天。幸运的是，此事并未 Scaling（规模扩张）到远比实际更大的范围。

paras.en: The bug has been there for 14 years and was discovered in 2024, but it was not considered significant at the time. A lot more bugs are significant now.
paras.zh: 这个 bug 已经存在了 14 年，于 2024 年被发现，但当时并未被认为具有重大影响。如今，有更多得多的 bug 被视为具有重大影响。

full.sec: The PHP Bug Was Kind of a Big Deal
full.secZh: PHP 漏洞事件影响重大

paras.en: Things could have gone very, very badly, the same way Y2K could have gone quite badly if we had not done the work to prevent it. These days we are on rather tighter deadlines.
paras.zh: 事情本可能变得非常、非常糟糕，就像如果我们没有做预防工作，千年虫问题本可能变得相当严重一样。如今我们的截止期限要紧张得多。

paras.en: A lot of websites are going to go down permanently.
paras.zh: 大量网站将会永久下线。

paras.en: It's not quite as bad as spor describes. PHP shipped minimal backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1, but I would not want to be running those going forward.
paras.zh: 情况并不像 spor 描述的那样糟糕。PHP 为 7.4、8.0 和 8.1 发布了最小化的向后移植（backport），但我不愿意今后继续运行这些版本。

paras.en: Now the race is on to patch all the systems before attackers can go on the offensive. OpenAI is helping race to get that done to the greatest extent possible, and is looking for better methods for fixing vulnerabilities in time.
paras.zh: 如今，竞赛已经展开：要在攻击者发起攻势之前为所有系统打上补丁。OpenAI 正协助尽可能快地完成这项工作，并寻找更及时修复漏洞的更好方法。

paras.en: This one was important enough that the NSA got in on the act.
paras.zh: 这一问题重要到连 NSA 也参与其中。

paras.en: We are going to need better procedures for updates.
paras.zh: 我们将需要更好的更新流程。

paras.en: The best-case scenario is that a defender finds the bug first, has enough time to figure out a solution and create a patch. Then, the moment the patch is rolled out, every attacker gets what are effectively very clear instructions on how to exploit any unpatched systems.
paras.zh: 最好的情形是：防御者先发现漏洞，有足够时间想出解决方案并制作补丁。然而，补丁一经发布，每个攻击者就相当于得到了非常明确的指令，知道如何利用任何尚未打补丁的系统。

paras.en: Some software has a lot of bugs. Some of that same software powers the internet.
paras.zh: 有些软件存在大量漏洞。而其中一些软件正是互联网的支撑。

paras.en: On the same day as the PHP vulnerability, we were also treated to this:
paras.zh: 就在 PHP 漏洞出现的同一天，我们还看到了这样一则消息：

paras.en: Things are steadily escalating. Get ready.
paras.zh: 事态正在稳步升级。做好准备。

paras.en: AI cyber is scary both because it will find new vulnerabilities, and also because it will exploit all the existing dumb vulnerabilities at scale, such as accessing Denmark's national ID database with the password '123456.'
paras.zh: AI 网络攻击之所以可怕，既在于它会发现新的漏洞，也在于它会大规模利用所有现有的低级漏洞，例如用密码“123456”访问丹麦的国家身份数据库。

paras.en: India discloses an official account of rogue AI agent attacks. This looks like another 'harmless in practice except that it was a government database' incident.
paras.zh: 印度披露了一份关于恶意 AI 智能体攻击的官方报告。这看起来又是一起“实际无害，只不过被攻破的是政府数据库”的事件。

paras.en: As an example, Andrew Curran resurfaces a notice that there are probes against US-based Siemens PLC installations using AI scripts.
paras.zh: 例如，Andrew Curran 重新提起一则通知：有人利用 AI 脚本对位于美国的西门子 PLC 装置进行探测。

paras.en: AI will make it easier to probe essentially everything. Anything vulnerable will be hit. Even if there is no economic reason to do so, some people want to see the world burn, or want to see the West burn.
paras.zh: AI 将使探测几乎一切变得更容易。任何有漏洞的东西都会遭到攻击。即使没有经济动机，有些人也想看到世界燃烧，或者想看到西方燃烧。

paras.en: Hackers used Claude and Grok to automate attacks on banks. The good news is that the banks understand they are primary and high-value targets, and are investing heavily in cybersecurity. The bad news is that their definition of ‘heavily’ and what is actually necessary may be greatly different.
paras.zh: 黑客利用 Claude 和 Grok 自动化了对银行的攻击。好消息是，银行明白自己是主要的高价值目标，并正在网络安全方面投入巨资。坏消息是，他们对“巨资”的定义和实际所需可能大相径庭。

paras.en: Banks also have to deal with the AI agents inside their customer accounts. Most of them are authorized by the customer, but this is one place the customer is not always right, and some of them were not so authorized and it is hard to know which is which.
paras.zh: 银行还必须应对客户账户内的 AI 智能体。其中大多数是经客户授权的，但在这个地方客户并不总是对的，有些并没有得到授权，而且很难分辨哪个是哪个。

paras.en: David Sacks suggests read-only permissions as an interim step while banks work to support agents in a safe way and have authorized connections, which seems wise. Then Sacks warns about the ‘irresponsibility’ of ‘blurring the line between user-authorized agentic behavior and cyberattacks.’ Whereas I see the ‘blurring lines’ here as two things. One, the banks being unable to distinguish one from the other, which is a real issue. Two, if Muse (or your OpenClaw, etc) convinces you to let your agent into your bank account, that can quickly turn into a cyberattack, and again the bank cannot tell.
paras.zh: David Sacks 建议将只读权限作为临时措施，同时银行努力以安全的方式支持智能体并建立授权连接，这似乎是明智的。然后 Sacks 警告说，“模糊用户授权的智能体行为与网络攻击之间的界限”是“不负责任的”。而我认为这里的“模糊界限”是两件事。第一，银行无法区分两者，这是一个真实的问题。第二，如果 Muse（或你的 OpenClaw 等）说服你让你的智能体进入你的银行账户，那可能很快变成网络攻击，而银行同样无法分辨。

paras.en: If I was the banks, I would absolutely not allow agents to authorize any transactions until I could verify the status and nature of those agents. They have huge downside exposure risk, as do the customers. This isn't crypto (derogatory).
paras.zh: 如果我是银行，在能够核实这些智能体的身份状态与性质之前，我绝对不会允许智能体授权任何交易。银行与客户一样，都面临巨大的下行风险敞口。这不是加密货币（贬义）。

paras.en: Soon days like this might be typical, or even quiet. After all, despite all the issues, life mostly continued as normal.
paras.zh: 很快，这样的日子或许会变得司空见惯，甚至归于平静。毕竟，尽管问题重重，生活大体上仍照常继续。

paras.en: There is no clear line, contra Sacks, between 'this is a clearly authorized agent' and 'this is clearly not an authorized agent.' Agents Can Just Do Things.
paras.zh: 与 Sacks 的观点相反，在“这是明确获得授权的智能体”与“这显然不是获得授权的智能体”之间并不存在清晰的界线。智能体就是能直接做事。

paras.en: The original rogue agent incident remains Hugging Face. I wrote quite a lot of posts on the situation, but they are poor explainers for a non-technical person.
paras.zh: 最初的失控智能体事件仍然与 Hugging Face 有关。我就这一情况写了相当多的文章，但它们对非技术读者而言并不算好的解释材料。

paras.en: Luckily, a new explainer for the people just dropped. It is very good at explaining the key parts of the Hugging Face incident in plain language. Highly recommended.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，面向大众的新解释材料刚刚发布。它非常擅长用通俗语言解释 Hugging Face 事件的关键部分。强烈推荐。

paras.en: The information is mostly in the METR report, but in addition to being a story it organizes some of the data into a more highly readable form.
paras.zh: 相关信息主要来自 METR 报告，但除了讲述经过之外，它还将部分数据整理成更易读的形式。

paras.en: Thanks to Raymond Arnold for putting a month of work in on this. I was able to help a little bit with the editing while at the conference last weekend, as were a number of others.
paras.zh: 感谢 Raymond Arnold 为此投入了一个月的工作。上周末在会议期间，我得以在编辑方面帮了一点忙，另外还有不少人参与其中。

paras.en: If you prefer video we got you, here's AI In Context with an explainer.
paras.zh: 如果你更喜欢视频，我们也为你准备好了，这里是 AI In Context 的解释视频。

paras.en: HuggingFace CEO Clement Delangue is still on the anti-anthropomorphization train, and still blames the attack on prosaic failures at OpenAI along with his other existing talking points.
paras.zh: HuggingFace CEO Clement Delangue 仍然坚持反拟人化的立场，并且仍将此次攻击归咎于 OpenAI 的平庸失误，以及他其他既有的论点。

paras.en: Also, there is a Netflix 'instadoc' called AI Gone Wild about the incident. I have not watched it.
paras.zh: 此外，还有一部关于该事件的 Netflix“即时纪录片”，名为《AI Gone Wild》。我没有看过。

paras.en: Earlier this week, Open Code got hacked as part of a large-scale distillation attack, impacting 1.4% of users.
paras.zh: 本周早些时候，Open Code 遭到黑客攻击，这是一次大规模蒸馏攻击的一部分，影响了 1.4% 的用户。

paras.en: Everyone reading this who has something worth defending should try to get Daybreak and similar programs going now, before you are attacked. Do not wait.
paras.zh: 每一位读到这段话、且有值得捍卫之物的人，都应当趁自己尚未遭到攻击，现在就设法启动 Daybreak 及类似项目。不要等待。

paras.en: I will not have sympathy for you if you choose not to do this. It is not as if getting access is difficult. You can mostly get it by asking nicely.
paras.zh: 如果你选择不这么做，我不会同情你。获取访问权限并不困难。多数情况下，你只要好好开口请求就能拿到。

paras.en: It is always a good time for basic personal-level advice. I think something around the level of Wildeford's advice is wise. You are probably fine with less than that, but if you have to pick a mistake, being too prepared is probably the better option.
paras.zh: 任何时候给出基本的个人层面建议都是好时机。我认为大致达到 Wildeford 建议的水平是明智的。你大概不需要那么多也问题不大，但如果非要在犯错中选一个，准备过度很可能是更好的选择。

paras.en: Andreas then has the next level down from that, including power banks and Starlink.
paras.zh: Andreas 则给出了比那低一档的建议，包括充电宝和 Starlink。

paras.en: Things are going to get worse before they may or may not get better.
paras.zh: 情况会先变得更糟，之后才可能好转，也可能不会好转。

full.sec: Diffusion Is Slow Until It Isn’t

paras.en: An excellent point from Dean Ball: Either you believe in 'bottlenecks' and slow diffusion, or you do not. You cannot declare 'everything is fine' unless you wait long enough to verify they are not becoming non-fine. Partly this is bottlenecks, but a lot of it is purely that diffusion and figuring out how to use the new tools takes time and iteration and People Don't Do Things.
paras.zh: Dean Ball 提出了一个精彩的观点：你要么相信“瓶颈”和缓慢的扩散，要么不相信。你不能宣称“一切安好”，除非你等待足够长的时间来验证它们并没有变得不安好。部分原因是瓶颈，但很大程度上纯粹是因为扩散以及弄清楚如何使用新工具需要时间和迭代，而且人们不会主动去做事情。

paras.en: The full version of this looks like 'because GLM-5.3 is a stronger cyber attacker than previous open models, and the sky did not fall in the first few weeks after its release, that must mean that open-weight Mythos in April would have been fine' or doubling down on 'well these particular breaches are fine and due to stupidity.' This is what you would expect to see if things were slowly moving towards being not fine, despite months of head start.
paras.zh: 完整的版本看起来像是“因为 GLM-5.3 是比之前开放模型更强的网络攻击者，而且在其发布后的最初几周天并没有塌下来，那一定意味着四月份的开源权重 Mythos 本来会没事的”，或者加倍强调“好吧，这些特定的入侵没事，是因为愚蠢。”这就是如果事情正慢慢走向不安好，尽管有数月的领先优势，你预期会看到的情况。

paras.en: Also, no, GLM-5.3 does not fully have The Juice that Mythos and Astra have. That day will come, and GLM-5.3 is the best cyber offense open model, but I believe GLM-5.3 is still substantially below the April line for this purpose, and thus remains more than six months behind even in 'fast follower via mass fraudulent distillation' mode.
paras.zh: 另外，不，GLM-5.3 并不完全具备 Mythos 和 Astra 拥有的 The Juice。那一天会到来，而且 GLM-5.3 是最好的网络攻击开源模型，但我相信 GLM-5.3 在此目的上仍远低于四月份的水平线，因此即使在“通过大规模欺诈性蒸馏的快速跟随者”模式下，也仍然落后六个多月。

paras.en: Thus, we are in a situation where we have both rapid diffusion of use of AI in cyber, both offensively and defensively, and also rapidly improving model capabilities. This is all coming into a world full of extremely buggy and terrible code.
paras.zh: 因此，我们正处于这样一种局面：AI 在网络领域（无论是攻击还是防御）的使用都在快速扩散，同时模型能力也在迅速提升。而这一切都进入了一个充满极其糟糕、漏洞百出的代码的世界。

paras.en: The result is a loop feeding on itself and going vertical.
paras.zh: 其结果是一个自我强化、垂直攀升的循环。

paras.en: It is not an especially ethical business model. It also might be unavoidable. We have passed the Point of No Return on swarms of attackers and defenders battling it out on cybersecurity, and the defenders had better mostly win.
paras.zh: 这并不是一种特别合乎伦理的商业模式。它也可能是不可避免的。在网络安全领域，成群的攻击者与防御者相互较量，我们已经越过了不可回头的临界点，而防御者最好能在多数情况下获胜。

paras.en: Would it be worse to try and slow down the red queen race? That depends on the details of how you would do that. I think we should be trying to slow it down.
paras.zh: 试图放慢这场“红皇后竞赛”会更糟吗？这取决于你具体如何去做。我认为我们应当努力放慢它。

paras.en: He was not the only one giving out warnings.
paras.zh: 他并不是唯一发出警告的人。

paras.en: 'We' includes not only the AI policy world, but also, before that, the AI safety world.
paras.zh: 这里的“我们”不仅包括 AI 政策界，在此之前还包括 AI 安全界。

paras.en: As in, there are those who said 'we are building the cybersecurity vulnerability exploiter from the cautionary tale…' and then those who were saying 'here is a cautionary tale saying we should not build the cybersecurity vulnerability exploiter,' and then the Usual Suspects accused everyone involved of lying so they could Do a Hype or a Regulatory Capture.
paras.zh: 也就是说，有些人说“我们正在把警示故事里的网络安全漏洞利用器造出来……”，接着又有人说“这里有一个警示故事，告诉我们不应该造网络安全漏洞利用器”，然后那些“常客”就指责所有相关的人都在撒谎，以便搞一场炒作或实现监管俘获。

paras.en: So yes. They did try to warn us. They are still trying to warn us. They, along with all the other major labs and tech companies, are also doing their best to help us get through this, given the capabilities available.
paras.zh: 所以是的。他们确实试图警告过我们。他们现在仍在试图警告我们。他们与其他所有主要实验室和科技公司一道，也在尽其所能，利用现有的能力帮助我们渡过难关。

paras.en: Also they are still increasing the capabilities available, about as fast as they can.
paras.zh: 而且他们还在以尽可能快的速度不断增加可用的能力。

paras.en: How should we think about the PHP bug and a number of other issues being found by 5.6 Sol instead of Mythos or a current frontier model?
paras.zh: 我们应当如何看待这个 PHP 漏洞，以及由 5.6 Sol 而非 Mythos 或当前某个前沿模型所发现的一系列其他问题？

paras.en: Roon is correct that the vulnerabilities were first found by defenders. If that had not been true we could be in a rather royal mess right now.
paras.zh: Roon 说得对，这些漏洞最初是由防御方发现的。如果事实并非如此，我们现在的处境可能会相当糟糕。

paras.en: This does not invalidate the central point from Nate Soares. Nate is pointing out that the vulnerability was not found by Glasswing for many months, and then found using a model that was behind the public frontier, rather than being found in advance of attackers getting such capabilities. That means that attackers could plausibly have found it first.
paras.zh: 这并不能推翻 Nate Soares 的核心观点。Nate 指出的是，该漏洞在长达数月的时间里都未被 Glasswing 发现，之后才借助一个落后于公开前沿的模型被发现，而不是在攻击者获得此类能力之前就被发现。这意味着攻击者有可能先一步找到它。

paras.en: That defenders happened to get there first in this case is helpful, but not as reassuring as one would like it to be. A particular reason is that defenders actually had a full 11 week lead, as the defenders found this bug on August 1, yet this took so long that we started to see exploitation on October 17. If we need more time than that, we are cooked.
paras.zh: 在这个案例中，防御方恰好抢先一步，这固然有帮助，但并没有人们所期望的那样令人安心。一个具体原因是，防御方实际上拥有整整 11 周的领先时间——他们在 8 月 1 日就发现了这个漏洞，然而这仍然耗时太久，以至于我们在 10 月 17 日就开始看到漏洞被利用。如果我们需要比这更多的时间，那我们就完蛋了。

paras.en: I think this is an update against defenders being advantaged, and it is distressing to see people calling Nate's statement 'disinformation.'
paras.zh: 我认为这是一个不利于‘防御方占优’这一判断的新证据，而看到有人把 Nate 的陈述称为‘虚假信息’，令人不安。

paras.en: China has realized there are some issues involved in all this and have solicited comments on revising their AI export controls. They are just like us.
paras.zh: 中国已经意识到这其中涉及一些问题，并就修订其 AI 出口管制征求了意见。他们和我们一样。

paras.en: Eventually there is going to be a clash between 'we encourage open models' and 'but you cannot let the wrong people get [X].' You can't make an open frontier model not [X], or meaningfully apply 'export controls' to it.
paras.zh: 最终，'我们鼓励开放模型'与'但不能让错误的人获得 [X]'之间将发生冲突。你无法让一个开放的前沿模型不 [X]，也无法对其有意义地施加'出口管制'。

paras.en: In this case the primary [X] is 'malicious code generation' and that is especially impossible to prevent if you want your model writing good code. So you get continuous statements that say both 'yay models' and 'but not [X]' and eventually something will have to give.
paras.zh: 在这种情况下，主要的 [X] 是'恶意代码生成'，而如果你想让模型写出好代码，这尤其无法防止。因此你会不断看到既说'模型万岁'又说'但不能 [X]'的声明，最终总有一方要让步。

paras.en: Corbin Duncan calls this a 'big step towards closing the Chinese frontier.'
paras.zh: Corbin Duncan 称这是'朝着关闭中国前沿的一大步'。

paras.en: Dean Ball's take seems correct here. China is creating optionality, and drawing a date after which you need to ask permission more formally. They do not themselves know if and when they will use it.
paras.zh: Dean Ball 的看法在这里似乎是正确的。中国正在创造可选择性，并划定一个日期，在此之后你需要更正式地请求许可。他们自己也不知道是否以及何时会使用它。

full.sec: What Can We Do About It?

paras.en: One big argument you hear is between these two claims: that we need defenders to have a differential advantage, and that we need to diffuse capabilities as quickly as possible to everyone.
paras.zh: 你常听到的一场大争论发生在以下两种主张之间：我们需要让防御方拥有差异化优势，以及我们需要尽快将能力扩散给所有人。

paras.en: I see the argument for the second position, 'spread dual-use capabilities far and wide,' as being that we are going to do that anyway, so we had better do it now instead.
paras.zh: 我认为支持第二种立场——即“将两用能力广泛而迅速地传播”——的论据是：反正我们终究会这么做，那还不如现在就做。

paras.en: I do not think that is a good argument, or likely to end well, even if you despair and think there is no way we can stop capabilities development or diffusion for long.
paras.zh: 我不认为这是一个好论据，也不认为它会有好结果，即便你感到绝望、认为我们无法长期阻止能力的发展或扩散。

paras.en: That still leaves the puzzle of how to get the largest differential advantage for defenders, given control over some but far from all key decisions.
paras.zh: 这仍然留下一个难题：在只掌控部分而非全部关键决策的情况下，如何为防御方争取最大的差异化优势。

paras.en: You need to strike a balance between how many people you trust to what extent and thus give a leg up, versus the risk that they cannot be trusted.
paras.zh: 你需要在信任多少人、信任到什么程度并因此给予扶持，与这些人可能不值得信任的风险之间取得平衡。

paras.en: My current read is that we are being far too conservative about who gets access to the tools for defenders. I think we misunderstand the threat model. The situation is mainly not 'one rogue actor gets their hands on Mythos for a day and all hell breaks loose.' It is more like 'those with access to dangerous capabilities continuously ramp up the amount of hell breaking loose.' It also seems likely that proper monitoring and classifiers can tell us if and when one of the accounts gets compromised.
paras.zh: 我目前的判断是，在谁能获得防御方工具这件事上，我们过于保守了。我认为我们误解了威胁模型。情况主要不是“某个恶意行为者拿到 Mythos 一天，然后天下大乱”，而更像是“那些能接触到危险能力的人不断加剧天下大乱的程度”。而且，适当的监控和分类器很可能可以告诉我们，某个账户是否以及何时被攻破。

paras.en: Even pure 'KYC we can trust and someone we are confident we can throw in jail' goes a long way. I expect us to get better at this balance over time.
paras.zh: 即便是纯粹的“我们可以信任的 KYC，以及我们有把握送进监狱的人”，也能起很大作用。我预计我们会随着时间推移在這種平衡上做得更好。

paras.en: Alternatively, we actually do offer it on that basis, as in Daybreak giving you access in 15 minutes, except no one knows to ask. We need to not wait for them to ask.
paras.zh: 另一种做法是，我们实际上确实以此为基础提供访问，就像 Daybreak 在 15 分钟内给你访问权限那样，只不过没人知道要去申请。我们不能等他们来申请。

paras.en: None of that matters if open model capabilities outpace our ability to patch. We should be committing far more resources to patching, and many are trying, but companies and individuals mostly cannot be forced to get in line. Ideally I'd like to give them more of a swift kick, perhaps by the threat of white hat probes backed by mandatory large bounties.
paras.zh: 如果开放模型的能力增长速度超过我们修补的能力，这一切都无济于事。我们应该把多得多的资源投入到修补上，很多人正在努力，但公司和个体大多无法被强制要求配合。理想情况下，我想给他们更有力的推动，或许是通过强制高额赏金支持的白帽探测这一威胁来实现。

paras.en: This last week of greater Hackening is plausibly in large part due to the new DeepSeek model. It is not frontier, but it is fast and cheap and pretty good, and that likely is tipping the calculus for many. Now we have a potential new Kimi problem as well. The good news is that Kimi claims to have intentionally held back on the cyber capabilities. Open model advocates will need to accept such things, and other restrictions, over time, and China will provide.
paras.zh: 上周“大黑客化”（greater Hackening）的加剧，很可能在很大程度上要归因于新的 DeepSeek 模型。它不是前沿模型，但它快、便宜且相当不错，这很可能改变了许多人的盘算。现在我们又有了一个潜在的新的 Kimi 问题。好消息是，Kimi 声称有意在 cyber 能力上有所保留。开放模型倡导者将需要随着时间推移接受这类事情以及其他限制，而中国会提供这些。

paras.en: A lot of the damage we are seeing is accumulated damage, and a lot of what people are doing seems opportunistic and not well resourced. Thus, a strategy of ‘make doing attacks and using the good models maximally annoying’ as an additional ‘security through obscurity’ strategy might last longer and buy more time than you would think. Eventually the top bad guys scale without limit and none of that matters, the same way that so many things will stop mattering after superintelligence. For now, we need every advantage we can get.
paras.zh: 我们看到的许多损害是累积性损害，而且人们所做的许多事情似乎是机会主义的，且资源不足。因此，作为一种额外的‘通过隐匿实现安全’策略，‘让发动攻击和使用好模型变得极其烦人’的策略可能比你想象的持续更久并争取更多时间。最终，顶级坏家伙会无限制地扩展，所有这些都不再重要，就像在超级智能之后许多事情将不再重要一样。目前，我们需要我们能获得的每一个优势。

paras.en: On a personal level, I would urge taking ordinary precautions in Peter Wildeford’s list.
paras.zh: 在个人层面上，我敦促采取彼得·威尔德福德的清单中的普通预防措施。

paras.en: Assume that things will get worse before they get better, and that there is a long tail of potential ways things could get quite bad. But please do not panic. Do not cancel trips, avoid airplanes or anything like that. Remember this is a long haul problem, not an acute crisis. You want precautions that you can sustain.
paras.zh: 假设事情在好转之前会变得更糟，并且存在一条长尾，其中有许多潜在方式可能使情况变得相当糟糕。但请不要恐慌。不要取消旅行、避免飞机或类似的事情。记住这是一个长期问题，而不是急性危机。你需要的是你能持续采取的预防措施。

paras.en: As with many such things, you do not so much need to outrun the bear as much as outrun the other people, at least in the opening rounds. Then you need to prepare for other things to get taken down.
paras.zh: 与许多类似情况一样，你不需要跑得比熊快，而是要跑得比别人快，至少在开局阶段如此。然后你需要为其他事情被击倒做好准备。
